events.description: Zalmay Khalilzad gives 9-10 hour transcribed interview to House Foreign Affairs Committee; claims AQIS 'dismantled', Afghan government expected to last 2+ years, calls Zawahiri in Haqqani house 'a violation, full and complete'
HFAC releases 284-page transcript of Khalilzad interview
Khalilzad appointed Special Representative for Afghanistan Reconciliation; decision to withdraw already made by Aug 2018
Joscelyn publishes 'The War in Afghanistan is Over, We Lost'
US drone strike kills Zawahiri in Haqqani safe house in Kabul
Khalilzad tweets that Taliban are delivering on Doha commitments to fight ISIS and prevent AQ use of Afghan soil
Kabul falls to Taliban; Roggio had predicted government would not survive the summer
Kabul airport attack kills 13 Americans during chaotic withdrawal
Roggio and Khalilzad testify at HFAC subcommittee hearing 'Pakistan: friend or foe'; Khalilzad says Taliban will never break with AQ and Pakistan will always support Taliban
Taliban publicly state they will not share power with the Afghan government
CENTCOM commander Kurilla testifies reduced ISR means campaign against AQ and ISIS-K 'is challenged'
Gen. McKenzie says US intelligence capacity in Afghanistan reduced to 1-2% of pre-withdrawal
US raid on AQ camp at Shorabak, Kandahar kills 150-200 AQ fighters, contradicting DoD 50-100 estimate confined to northeast
Short-lived Taliban ceasefire (Eid) which Gen. Nicholson took pride in; Taliban claim it was unilateral
McMaster-era South Asia strategy promising a path to victory; abandoned by 2018
Doha agreement signed; 5,000 Taliban prisoners released; 'window dressing' for a decided withdrawal

key_claims: The US decision to withdraw was made by Aug 2018; Khalilzad's Doha process was 'window dressing' that became complicit in selling the lie that the Taliban would break with al-Qaeda and negotiate with Kabul.
Khalilzad's claim that AQIS has been 'dismantled' is contradicted by UN reporting of AQ camps in 10 (hosts: at least 13) provinces; AQIS is simply absorbed into the emirate.
Khalilzad's own assessment that the Afghan government would last 2+ years is a 'game-ender' for his credibility; Kabul fell within months.

The Haqqanis are an integral part of the Taliban: Siraj Haqqani and Mullah Yaqoob (Kandahari) both knew of Zawahiri's Kabul safe house, so Hibatullah almost certainly did too; the Kandahari-vs-Haqqani dichotomy is false.
Taliban fighting ISIS has nothing to do with Doha; the real test, breaking with al-Qaeda, was failed.
In 2016 Khalilzad testified the Taliban would never break with AQ and Pakistan would always back the Taliban; by 2018 he claimed the opposite without explanation.
Khalilzad dismissed the UN Monitoring Team and questioned the (Indonesian) committee chair's nationality; hosts trust UN reports' track record over US assessments.
US intelligence on Afghanistan is now 1-2% of pre-withdrawal capacity; past assessments (50-100 AQ, confined to northeast) were disproven by the 2015 Shorabak raid.
Biden could have discarded the Doha deal (Khalilzad admits it was an option) but chose to follow through; Biden owns the final act.
